verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "I woke up this morning about an hour ago and I couldn't move my left arm anymore" and "I feel no pain, but just can't move it."
Persistence is confirmed when asked later: "Have you got the symptoms right now? Still. The arm?" Patient replies: "Yes, yes. The. The arm still can't move."
Patient says: "I feel a bit of tingling on the left side of my face" and when asked duration: "Since I woke up… So an hour ago."

Patient notes dribbling and swallowing difficulty: "I was trying to drink earlier and I dribbled a bit"; Doctor clarifies "you had some difficulty swallowing, is that right?" and patient responds "Yeah." Mildness is a reasonable inference.
In response to question about speech: Patient states, "Yeah, it feels a bit harder. It's more complicated. Maybe be more slow. I need to think more about it."
Doctor asks about asymmetry: "have you noticed any kind of asymmetry in your face… Anything different at all?" Patient replies, "No, not really."
Doctor asks: "Have you had any symptoms in your left leg at all?" Patient responds, "No."
On other illnesses, patient says: "I have type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure."
Same line: "I have type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure." Hypertension = high blood pressure.
In response to medication question, patient states: "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
Same response includes: "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
Same response includes: "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
Doctor asks about medication allergies; patient says: "Only penicillin, I believe."
On family illnesses, patient says: "My dad has got heart disease, but I don't know. More detail."
Doctor asks: "And are you normally living alone?" Patient replies, "Yes."
Doctor asks, "Do you smoke at all?" Patient replies, "I used to." This supports that he is an ex-smoker.
On alcohol, patient says: "I will have a few drinks over the weekend, maybe a couple more during the week." When asked what drinks: "Beers. Like pints."
Self-assessed facial symmetry: to question about asymmetry, patient replies, "No, not really."
Doctor asks: "And is there any discoloration in your hand?" Patient: "No." Doctor: "Does your hand feel cold?" Patient: "Not really. The arm feels fine apart from me not be able to move it."
Initial complaint: "I couldn't move my left arm anymore" and later: "The arm still can't move."

Transcript documents acute left arm paralysis, left facial tingling, dysphagia ("difficulty swallowing" with dribbling), and dysarthria (slower, harder speech), and doctor states: "I'm concerned that some of the symptoms you've got may be some symptoms of a stroke."
Type 2 diabetes is in past medical history: "I have type 2 diabetes" and is appropriately included in assessment.
Hypertension ("high blood pressure") is in past medical history: "I have type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure" and is appropriately included in assessment.

Doctor: "I'm going to arrange one of my colleagues next to me to call an ambulance to your home address now" and later: "they'll probably take you down to the local hospital, a e. And they will ring through for the stroke doctor… to assess you…"

Doctor advises: "maybe you could leave the front door unlocked to sit in the hallway" and later: "Just make sure that the front door is open. Sit in the hallway by the front door so that they've got access."

Doctor says: "what I'm going to do is I'm going to stay on the line until they reach there Just to make sure that you're okay" and again: "I'm just going to stay on the line, and we'll. And we'll wait until the ambulance comes."
Same as above: patient is instructed implicitly to remain on the phone as doctor states, "I'm going to stay on the line until they reach there" and "we'll wait until the ambulance comes."
